title: Run It Backwards
idea: An inverse function undoes the original, taking each output back to the input that made it.
misconceptions: Reads f⁻¹(x) as the reciprocal of f(x)
Computes f(a) when f⁻¹(a) is asked for

estimate.basis: 150 spoken words a minute, plus each pause, 0.8 s for each cue and 2 s for each tap question with its longer feedback line. The two figures are the two recall versions. Player turns are player-paced and not counted.

notes: Builds on ex.functions.function-machine, Rook's own, so the recall uses his own.watched, own.not-watched, short-version and after lines.

No second-method section: the map lists no methods. Three of the skill's four methods are in the script: reversing the flow diagram is the big idea and example 1, solving f(x) = a is example 2 and example 3(c), and swapping coordinates is the end of the big idea and example 3(b).

The skill's fourth method, reflecting the graph in y = x, is the map's next explainer, ex.functions.inverse-reflection (The Mirror Line), so the recap points there and the reflection misconception is left to it. Finding f⁻¹(x) as a formula is ex.functions.swap-and-solve (AA, and AI HL).

The turns use fn-graph-table-composite-inverse, the only question type with SL2.2.inverse-undo whose chain reads an inverse value. Its live version gives a graph or a table, so turn 1 may arrive as a table rather than a rule. Phase 2 (turns and the engine, with Coder) should check that the twin still mirrors example 1. The fallbacks are fixed and worked below.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Seventeen came out. To find what went in, run the line backwards. Two things flip. The order flips, so the last thing done is the first undone. And each step flips: add becomes take away, times becomes divide.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Seventeen, take away three, fourteen. Fourteen, halved, seven. Seven went in.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Check it forwards. Seven doubled is fourteen, plus three, seventeen. Loud and clear.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: The machine that runs f backwards is the inverse function. It's written f, with a small minus one up top, and you say f inverse. f inverse of seventeen is seven.

f⁻¹(17) = 7: the input that f turns into 17

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: That minus one isn't a power. f inverse of seventeen isn't one over f of seventeen. It's a label. It means run f backwards.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: And if f sends seven to seventeen, f inverse sends seventeen back to seven, so every pair swaps round, input for output, and a table for f inverse is f's table with its two rows swapped. Sorry. Back on frequency.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: My oupa said undoing is like getting dressed for the cold. Socks, then boots. So boots come off first. He tested it the other way once.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Step two: the rule as a line of operations. Times four, then take away five.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Step three: run it backwards. Undo the minus five first. Twenty-three plus five, twenty-eight.

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air

problem.setup: The table shows some values of a function f. x: −1, 0, 2, 3, 5. f(x): 7, 4, −2, −5, −11.

parts.text: The function is f(x) = 4 − 3x. Find f⁻¹(25).

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Paper style now. A table of values for a function f. Inputs on the top row, outputs on the bottom.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Part a. Write down f of two. Find two in the input row, and read down. Two in, minus two out. Write down means no working needed.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Part b. Write down f inverse of four.

ask.prompt: For f⁻¹(4), which row do you find 4 in?

right.speaker: rook-dead-air

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Four is in the output row, under zero. f of zero is four, so f inverse of four is zero.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Part c. Twenty-five isn't in the table, so we use the rule. Before solving, a prediction. The outputs go up as the inputs go down, so an output of twenty-five should come from an input below minus one. f inverse of twenty-five is the input that gives twenty-five.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Take four off both sides. Minus three x is twenty-one. Divide by minus three. x is minus seven.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Check forwards. Minus three times minus seven is twenty-one. Four plus twenty-one, twenty-five. And minus seven is below minus one, as predicted. Out.
